subject: dermatology
title: Acne vulgaris and rosacea: pilosebaceous pathogenesis, grading, stepped topical therapy, systemic retinoids

steps.tx: **Acne vulgaris** is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the pilosebaceous unit. Four interrelated pathogenic factors drive disease: follicular hyperkeratinisation causing microcomedone formation, androgen-driven sebaceous gland hypersecretion, proliferation of Cutibacterium acnes within sebum-rich follicles, and host immune-mediated inflammation. Lesions span non-inflammatory open and closed comedones to inflammatory papules, pustules, and deep nodules.
steps.say: Acne vulgaris arises from follicular hyperkeratinisation, androgenic sebum excess, Cutibacterium acnes proliferation, and host inflammation.

nodes.label: Sebum excess and C. acnes growth

steps.tx: **Stepped management of acne** aligns with clinical severity. Mild comedonal acne responds to topical retinoids (adapalene, tretinoin) targeting abnormal keratinocyte desquamation. Mild-to-moderate inflammatory acne requires combination therapy with **benzoyl peroxide** (which prevents bacterial resistance) plus a topical retinoid or topical antibiotic. Moderate-to-severe disease necessitates oral tetracyclines paired with topical benzoyl peroxide.
steps.say: Mild acne uses topical retinoids and benzoyl peroxide, stepping up to oral tetracyclines for inflammatory disease.

rows: Oral lymecycline or doxycycline plus topical

steps.tx: **Oral isotretinoin** is the only curative agent targeting all four pathogenic mechanisms of acne vulgaris. It induces profound sebaceous gland atrophy, normalizes follicular keratinisation, and reduces inflammation. Because isotretinoin is a potent human **teratogen** causing severe craniofacial, cardiac, and central nervous system malformations, strict pregnancy prevention programmes with reliable contraception are mandatory.
steps.say: Oral isotretinoin targets all four acne mechanisms, but is severely teratogenic, requiring strict pregnancy prevention programmes.

vis.caption: Isotretinoin targets all four acne pathogenic factors; potent teratogen

steps.tx: **Rosacea** is a chronic neurovascular facial disorder characterized by centrofacial erythema, flushing, telangiectasia, and inflammatory papules and pustules without comedones. Four major clinical subtypes are recognized: erythematotelangiectatic, papulopustular, phymatous (rhinophyma with sebaceous hyperplasia on the nose), and ocular rosacea. Sunlight, hot beverages, spicy foods, and alcohol frequently trigger flares.
steps.say: Rosacea produces centrofacial erythema, telangiectasia, and pustules without comedones, triggered by heat, sun, and alcohol.

steps.tx: **Rosacea management** combines avoidance of known thermal and dietary triggers with targeted topical and systemic therapy. Mild papulopustular rosacea responds to topical ivermectin, metronidazole, or azelaic acid. Moderate-to-severe disease requires sub-antimicrobial or standard-dose oral doxycycline. Topical brimonidine provides temporary vasoconstriction for persistent facial erythema.
steps.say: Management of rosacea requires trigger avoidance and topical ivermectin or metronidazole, stepping to oral doxycycline when severe.
